Subject: Clarify conditional transfer clauses and routing for TIA scope - MedCore pilot

Alice —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. As we start scoping the TIA/DTIA for the pilot, a couple of items popped up from our side that affect routing and subprocessor commitments:

1) Conditional transfer clause: MedCore mentioned a preference for an onshore-only path for EU-origin data in certain clinical flows. Can you confirm whether that is an absolute requirement (i.e., no routing to US infrastructure at any point) or a contractual preference that can be met via technical safeguards (e.g., dedicated region, pseudonymisation, strict logging)?

2) Subprocessor residency: Your team requested that certain logging and telemetry be processed in the EU. We attached our current Subprocessor-Map.xlsx — can you flag which processors you would need to be onshore or applicable to the TIA carve-out?

3) Evidence for UK/EEA controls: if MedCore requires a UK addendum + SCCs plus the TIA, what minimum artifacts should we include in the initial evidence pack to accelerate legal review?

I attached the latest MedCore-TIA-draft_v3.pdf and the subprocessor map. Kimberly from Legal is looped to confirm contract language options. If easier, we can set a 30-minute call next week to walk the legal team through routing variants.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MedCore-TIA-draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 312KB), Subprocessor-Map.xlsx (Excel, 46KB)

From: Alice McKay <alice.mckay@medcorehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify conditional transfer clauses and routing for TIA scope - MedCore pilot

Diego —

Thanks for sending these along and for the call earlier. Quick answers from our side to help you triage:  

- Onshore requirement: For PHI-derived transcripts and anything tied to identified patient flows we need European processing and storage; we can accept temporary US-based inference for non-identifying model tuning if data is pseudonymised and KV caches are segregated, but that needs explicit language in the TIA. In short: not strictly absolute, but contractually gated.

- Subprocessors: I flagged two rows in Subprocessor-Map.xlsx that are blockers for our InfoSec team (the analytics vendor and audit logs vendor). Both need EU data residency or an alternate provider.

- Evidence: Our legal team wants a combined package: (1) SCCs + mapping showing data flows, (2) TIA with routing carve-outs called out, (3) KMS/Encryption attestation, and (4) a short-run playbook describing fallback routing if EU capacity is saturated. A compact pack reduces our review from 4 weeks to ~10 business days.

I'll ask legal to provide a redline for the TIA and circle back once they confirm the exact addendum language for the onshore carve-out. Happy to do a cross-team call.

—Alice
Alice McKay
Director, Data Governance
MedCore Health

Hi Alice / Diego —

Appreciate the clarity, Alice. A few notes from Legal/Privacy after a quick review: 

- Contract language: we can include a conditional routing clause that requires onshore (EU/UK) processing for "Covered Clinical Data" as defined in the TIA. The clause will:
  * Define triggers (e.g., data tagged as PHI, patient identifiers present)
  * Require Redwood to keep EU-resident primary storage for covered data and to only use non-EU inference as a fallback with technical safeguards and customer authorization.

- SCCs / UK IDTA: for the combined SCCs + UK addendum path, we will prepare a short schedule of evidence (data flow diagram, encryption attestations, subprocessors with region columns). That schedule will be bundled as Exhibit B to the TIA.

- Operational fallback: we can draft a playbook clause that mandates notification windows (e.g., 1 hour SLA to notify MedCore of fallback, 24-hour mitigation plan) and limits fallback duration to a maximum number of hours per month unless mutually agreed. This should satisfy InfoSec gate concerns while preserving capacity flexibility.

- Subprocessor alternatives: Diego, please work with infra to propose EU-hosted replacements for the two flagged vendors or provide compensating controls (encryption-in-use for logs, contractually limited access). If not possible, we will list them as restricted subprocessors and include a remediation timeline in the TIA.

I'll attach a clean TIA that incorporates these options for your review. If acceptable, we can produce a redline showing the conditional routing clause and a trimmed evidence pack for MedCore legal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
